assignments.reason: This concept — 'when there is good in speech' — describes a qualitative state of dibur (speech). Its essential nature is a property of speech itself, which is the domain of malkhut-peh. The goodness here is the tov that makes speech receivable; it IS a state of speech, not something external to it.

Speech that is heard and accepted is the perfected state of dibur — speech functioning at its highest capacity. Its essential nature is speech/malkhut in its rectified, effective form. It is not the cause of speech nor the da'at that feeds it, but speech itself in its ideal mode.

Israel's closeness to their Father in Heaven is the ultimate purpose and culmination of the tikun haklali system. The text states explicitly: 'the main closeness of Israel to their Father in Heaven is through tikun habrit.' While it is an effect of tikun, its essential nature is inseparable from the tikun-rectification domain — it is what tikun IS for, the telos of the entire rectifying force represented by the tzaddik, the covenant, and the eagle.

assignments.node_id: שבח הצדיקים. כשמשבחין ומפארין את הצדיקים
assignments.reason: Praising the tzaddikim is essentially a practice centered on the tzaddik — it belongs to the domain of the tzaddik/tikun by its very nature. The act of praising IS engagement with the tzaddik-reality. Package 1 already contains צדיק, קשת הברית, and רוח as aspects of the same rectifying force. Praising the tzaddik is the human activation of that same domain.

Da'at (awareness/knowledge) raised and elevated is the mochin in their awakened, expanded state. The text equates this with 'awakening the mochin from their dormancy' — kaneshser ya'ir kino = kneh chokhma kneh bina = the mochin. Elevating da'at IS the mochin being restored to gadlut. Its essential nature is the cognitive-spiritual faculty (Package 2), now in its positive/elevated form.

Taking speech from da'at is the method of elevating speech. The text frames it as the answer to 'how does one make the good in speech?' — the subject and object are both speech. Its essential nature is a speech-practice: a way of perfecting dibur by connecting it to its source. The da'at here is the means, but the concept itself lives in the speech/malkhut domain.

Making good in speech is the process of perfecting the dibur itself. Its essential nature is entirely within the domain of speech — it describes the act of rectifying malkhut-peh. It IS speech-perfection, not something external that happens to produce good speech.

assignments.node_id: תקון הכללי שמעורר המחין כנ"ל, וממשיך לבנונית להגידין
assignments.reason: This is a descriptive variant of tikun haklali — the general rectification described in its full function (awakening the mochin and drawing whiteness to the sinews). Its essential nature is the tikun haklali itself, which is the core of Package 1. The description adds detail but does not change its identity.

Another descriptive variant equating tikun haklali with tikun habrit. Both concepts already exist in Package 1 (תקון הכללי and תקון הברית). This compound node_id in the dataset represents the same essential reality — the general/covenant rectification.

The 'falling sickness' in this Torah is explicitly the falling of the Shekhinah — sukat David hanofalat. Being healed from it means the Shekhinah/malkhut is restored from her fallen state. Its essential nature is the restoration of malkhut, which is the core of Package 3. The Torah connects this directly: 'and then the dibur is permitted' — the restoration of malkhut enables speech.

assignments.node_id: נתתקן ממילא כל הלאוין שעבר, ונמשך להם לבנונית
assignments.reason: The automatic rectification of all transgressions and the drawing of whiteness to them is the operative result of tikun haklali. Its essential nature is the tikun-rectification domain — it describes what the tikun haklali DOES, which is inseparable from what tikun haklali IS. The whitening (labnonut) flowing to the sinews is the core mechanism of the tikun system in Package 1.

assignments.node_id: יכון בכל הלוך והלוך, ובכל דבור ודבור, שהוא הולך ומדבר בשעת המשא ומתן, שכונתו כדי שירויח כדי שיתן צדקה
assignments.reason: The intention to direct all business profit toward tzedakah is essentially a practice of tzedakah — righteous giving. The text explicitly calls this 'the tikun haklali of the bloods' and equates tzedakah with klaliut hagiddin. Since tzedakah is already in Package 1 as a face of the tikun principle, this charitable-intention-in-commerce belongs to the same domain. Its essential nature is the tzedakah/tikun principle applied to the commercial sphere.

Commerce/business (masa umatan) is the earthly vehicle of livelihood/parnassah. Package 6 already contains ממון (money), מן (manna), and לחם מן השמים (bread from heaven) — the sustenance domain. Masa umatan is the practical, worldly form of parnassah. It is neutral because it can serve either holiness (when directed toward tzedakah) or corruption (when driven by greed/gezelah). Its essential nature is the livelihood domain.

Sustenance without toil is the ideal, divinely-granted form of parnassah — the very essence of Package 6. The text equates it directly with lechem min hashamayim and the manna. Its essential nature is heavenly sustenance, the core concept of Package 6.
